title: Ignition Failure (Prestige/Solo)
shortDescription: Burner failed to establish flame after the allowed retries.
fullDescription:
E01 on Triangle Tube Prestige and Solo condensing boilers indicates that ignition was attempted three times and flame was never proven. The boiler hard locks until reset.

Most common causes are closed gas valve, fouled ignition rod, plugged condensate trap, or low gas-supply pressure under load.
safetyWarning: Gas appliance — if you smell gas, evacuate and call the gas emergency line.

fixSteps.title: Verify gas
fixSteps.instruction: Make sure the gas valve at the boiler is open.

fixSteps.title: Reset
fixSteps.instruction: Press Reset on the ACVMax control and observe.

fixSteps.title: Clean ignition rod
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, remove, clean and gap.

whenToCallPro: Gas pressure work needs a manometer and licensed tech.

faq.a: Two resets is plenty; if E01 returns again, schedule service.

title: Flame Detected With Gas Off
shortDescription: Ionization signal seen when gas valve should be closed.
fullDescription: E02 indicates the flame-supervision circuit detects flame outside the valid burn window. This can mean a stuck gas valve or a flame-rod insulation problem.
safetyWarning: If gas odor present, treat as a gas leak emergency.

fixSteps.title: Inspect ignition assembly
fixSteps.instruction: Look for cracked porcelain or a chafed lead.

whenToCallPro: Gas valve replacement is pro-only.

faq.a: Yes — moisture is a frequent culprit on Prestige Solo.

title: Air Pressure Switch Stuck
shortDescription: APS stuck closed at start of cycle.
fullDescription: E03 means the air-pressure switch was closed before the inducer started — interpreted as welded contacts or a wiring short.
safetyWarning: Do not bypass the APS.

fixSteps.title: Inspect wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Check the APS leads for shorts.

fixSteps.title: Replace switch
fixSteps.instruction: Swap with OEM Triangle Tube APS.

whenToCallPro: If wire issue is in the harness.

title: Air Pressure Switch Open
shortDescription: APS did not close after fan ramp.
fullDescription: E04 means the inducer is running but the APS never closed. Look at intake/exhaust and the silicone hose for issues.
safetyWarning: Vent obstruction can cause CO spillage.
whenToCallPro: Blower replacement.

faq.a: Yes — clear snow well below terminations in winter.

title: High Limit Trip
fullDescription: E05 indicates the manual-reset high limit opened. Check for air-bound HX, failed circulator, or closed isolation valve.
safetyWarning: Do not bypass the high limit.

fixSteps.title: Bleed
fixSteps.instruction: Vent the HX and high points.

whenToCallPro: Pump replacement.

title: Low Water / LWCO
fullDescription: E06 means the LWCO probe has detected insufficient water. Refill to spec and check for leaks.
safetyWarning: Never bypass the LWCO.
whenToCallPro: Hidden leak or LWCO replacement.

faq.a: No — sealed systems should not need that.

title: Outlet Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Boiler outlet NTC out of range.
fullDescription: E07 covers the supply NTC. The boiler will not fire if the sensor is faulty.
safetyWarning: Power off before sensor work.

fixSteps.title: Reseat
fixSteps.instruction: Reseat the connector at the ACVMax.

fixSteps.title: Replace
fixSteps.instruction: Replace with OEM Triangle Tube sensor.

whenToCallPro: Drain/refill.

title: Return Sensor Fault
fullDescription: E08 covers the inlet/return sensor. The control needs both supply and return for HX protection.
safetyWarning: Power off before sensor work.
whenToCallPro: Drain/refill.

title: Outdoor Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Outdoor reset sensor open or shorted.
fullDescription: E10 is the outdoor sensor fault on Prestige Solo. The boiler reverts to fixed setpoint.
safetyWarning: No safety hazard.

fixSteps.title: Inspect cable
fixSteps.instruction: Walk the run looking for breaks.

whenToCallPro: Tall ladder access only.

title: Blower Fault
fullDescription: E15 indicates the fan tach feedback does not match commanded RPM. Debris or aged motor are common.
safetyWarning: Disconnect power before fan work.
whenToCallPro: Blower replacement.

title: Hard lockout
fullDescription: Persistent fault — service required. Common diagnostic code on Triangle Tube boiler. Resolve by following manufacturer service procedure for the implicated subsystem.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect power for 10 minutes, then restore.

fixSteps.title: Inspect
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect the implicated component, wiring, and connectors.

fixSteps.title: Test/replace
fixSteps.instruction: Test sensor with multimeter or replace if reading abnormal.

fixSteps.title: Verify
fixSteps.instruction: Restore power, clear codes, run system to verify.

safetyWarning: Gas/electric appliance — turn off gas and disconnect electrical power before servicing.
whenToCallPro: Gas-appliance work usually requires licensed HVAC tech.

faq.a: Resolve before continued use to prevent damage or safety hazard.

title: Outlet Sensor Open
fullDescription: Triangle Tube E21 is an open boiler outlet sensor. The boiler cannot fire safely.
whenToCallPro: If sensor checks good, call a tech.

title: Outlet Sensor Short
fullDescription: E22 short on outlet sensor. Replace sensor.
whenToCallPro: Persistent short means wiring damage.

title: Return Sensor Open
fullDescription: E23 indicates open return-side sensor.
whenToCallPro: If sensor checks good, call a tech.

title: Return Sensor Short
fullDescription: E24 short on return sensor.
whenToCallPro: Persistent short means wiring damage; call a tech.

title: Flue Sensor Open
fullDescription: E25: open flue thermistor.
whenToCallPro: If sensor checks good, call a tech.

title: Flue Sensor Short
fullDescription: E26 is the short-circuit counterpart to E25.
whenToCallPro: Persistent short = wiring damage.

title: Outdoor Sensor Open
fullDescription: E27 open outdoor sensor; outdoor reset inactive.
whenToCallPro: If sensor checks good, call a tech.

title: Outdoor Sensor Short
fullDescription: E28 short on outdoor sensor.
whenToCallPro: If sensor checks good, call a tech.

title: Tank Sensor Fault
fullDescription: E29 means the indirect water heater tank sensor is open, shorted, or out of range. DHW priority is disabled.
whenToCallPro: If sensor checks good, call a tech.

title: Pump Output Fault
shortDescription: Boiler cannot drive primary pump output.
fullDescription: E30 indicates an issue with the boiler's pump output — open coil on an external pump relay or PCB output failure.

fixSteps.title: Verify Pump Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Check that pump wiring matches schematic.

fixSteps.title: Test Output
fixSteps.instruction: Have a tech meter the boiler pump output.

whenToCallPro: Pump output faults usually need PCB replacement; call a tech.
